(3) Offline RL training methods for learning planners with reasoning as our core algorithmic contributions, which consistently improve over the Edit-Only baseline in visual quality and instruction following. (4) Comprehensive evaluation across 4B and 8B parameter Qwen3-VL models showing that our methods outperform other baselines in the majority of compositional tasks, validated by human evaluations.
items.author: Subhojyoti Mukherjee, Stefano Petrangeli, Branislav Kveton, Trung Bui, Franck Dernoncourt, Arko Mukherjee

items.title: SHERLOC: Statistical Hypothesis Evaluation and Recovery for Learning Opponent Characteristics
items.summary:
arXiv:2603.05625v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: When used in automated decision-making systems, machine learning (ML) models are vulnerable to data-manipulation attacks. Some defense mechanisms (e.g., adversarial regularization) directly affect the ML models while others (e.g., anomaly detection) act within the broader system. However, many defenses operate under a predefined threat model that assumes characteristics of the adversary, including their knowledge, capabilities, and objectives, are known and fixed. In practice, these characteristics may be unknown or evolve over time, creating a mismatch between the assumptions of the defender and the true attacker.
  In this paper, we study a new perspective on adversarial defense: focusing on the attacker, rather than the attack. We present and demonstrate SHERLOC, a framework for adversarial learning forensics -- namely, a detective that learns about the attacker from observed attack(s).
  We prove that, without additional knowledge, the attacker is non-identifiable --- multiple potential attackers would perform the same observed attack. This reveals an important distinction between reconstructing an attacker's behavior and recovering the attacker that generated it. We demonstrate empirically that SHERLOC is able to reconstruct a hypothesis attacker that is consistent with the observed attacks against various defender models (i.e., generalized least-squares linear regressors, logistic regressors, and polynomial classifiers) across various security-critical domains. Finally, we show that these inferred attackers need not match the ground truth attacker exactly to have downstream utility. Defenses using the SHERLOC-inferred attackers achieve approximately 90-100% of robustness improvement that would be achieved if the defender had access to the ground-truth attacker.
items.author: Soyon Choi, Scott Alfeld, Meiyi Ma

items.title: Stabilizing Policy Optimization via Logits Convexity
items.summary:
arXiv:2603.00963v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: While reinforcement learning (RL) has been central to the recent success of large language models (LLMs), RL optimization is notoriously unstable, especially when compared to supervised fine-tuning (SFT). In this work, we investigate the stability gap between SFT and RL from a gradient-based perspective, and show that the convexity of the SFT loss with respect to model logits plays a key role in enabling stable training. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that this property induces favorable gradient directionality during optimization. In contrast, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), a widely adopted policy gradient algorithm utilizing a clipped surrogate objective, lacks this stabilizing property. Motivated by this observation, we propose Logits Convex Optimization (LCO), a simple yet effective policy optimization framework that aligns the learned policy with an optimal target derived from the original RL objective, thereby emulating the stabilizing effects of logits-level convexity. Extensive experiments across multiple model families show that our LCO framework consistently improves training stability and outperforms conventional RL methods on a broad range of benchmarks.
items.author: Hongzhan Chen, Tao Yang, Yuhua Zhu, Shiping Gao, Xiaojun Quan, Ting Yao

items.title: Vectorized Dynamic Histograms for Sparse Oblique Forests
items.summary:
arXiv:2603.00326v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Sparse oblique (SPO), part of the top-ranked configuration of Google's Yggdrasil Decision Forests (YDF), improve the accuracy while maintaining interpretability of Random Forests (RF) and Gradient Boosted Trees (GBT) by scanning a sparse linear combination of features instead of a single feature. Because projections are sampled at runtime, training is significantly slower, as pre-run optimizations such as presorting cannot be used. We overhaul SPO training in YDF, first by fixing inefficiencies in the released version, achieving 2-5x speedup, then by devising two novel methods, one aimed at GBTs and the other at RFs: (1) Hierarchical AVX2 and AVX-512-vectorized histogram filling speeds up typical GBT-depth trees by up to 1.6x in SPO-GBT and 2x for SPO-RF, and (2) runtime-dynamic histograms between vectorized histograms and exact splits, speeds up deeper, RF depth-typical trees (depths 16 to purity) by up to 1.6x with no detectable effect on accuracy. Our optimizations bring SPO-RF training time on par with YDF's axis-aligned RF. We extensively evaluate on 8 natural and 11 synthetic datasets of up to 10.5 million rows and 1.6 million features, from depth 6 to purity, and open-source the implementation.
items.author: Ariel Lubonja, Jungsang Yoon, Haoyin Xu, Yue Wan, Yilin Xu, Richard Stotz, Mathieu Guillame-Bert, Joshua T. Vogelstein, Randal Burns

items.title: On objective mismatch in molecular retrieval from tandem mass spectrometry
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.16507v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Identifying molecular structures from LC-MS/MS spectra is a central problem in computational metabolomics, often approached by predicting molecular fingerprints and retrieving candidates via similarity search. Despite widespread use, the relationship between training objectives for fingerprint prediction and downstream retrieval performance remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate the alignment between these objectives and show that they can be misaligned under uncertainty. Adopting a decision-theoretic perspective, we derive novel regret bounds that characterize when Bayes-optimal predictors for fingerprint similarity diverge from those for molecular retrieval. Our analysis reveals that optimizing standard similarity-based losses can degrade retrieval performance, and that the extent of this mismatch depends on the similarity structure of candidate sets. Empirically, we validate our theory on the MassSpecGym and Enveda-180 datasets, observing a Pareto frontier between fingerprint accuracy and retrieval metrics across commonly used loss functions. These findings highlight potential trade-offs in fingerprint-based molecular identification and provide principled guidance for the design of learning objectives in small molecule mass spectrometry.
items.author: Gaetan De Waele, Marek Wydmuch, Krzysztof Dembczy\'nski, Wojciech Kot{\l}owski, Willem Waegeman

items.title: AnomaMind: Coarse-to-Fine Agentic Diagnosis via Hybrid Inference for Time Series Anomaly Detection
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.13807v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) supports the analysis of web service key performance indicators (KPIs) by identifying anomalous intervals. Recent large language model (LLM)-based agentic approaches have achieved promising results through reasoning and tool use. Despite their effectiveness, precise anomaly localization remains challenging, as diverse anomaly patterns demand targeted numerical evidence and iterative refinement to accurately determine anomaly boundaries. In this work, we propose AnomaMind, a coarse-to-fine agentic diagnosis framework for TSAD. AnomaMind first identifies suspicious regions from time-series visualizations, then adaptively acquires targeted numerical evidence through multi-turn tool interactions, and finally refines anomaly decisions through self-reflection. This process is supported by a tool engine that integrates knowledge memory and numerical analysis. To coordinate this diagnostic process, we design a hybrid inference strategy that employs frozen general-purpose LLMs for initial localization, tool orchestration, and evaluation, alongside a specialized LLM detector for evidence-grounded interval prediction. We optimize only the specialized detector through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on diagnostic trajectories and reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable detection rewards. Experiments on four benchmarks spanning web traffic, service KPIs, and system-monitoring signals, under both in-domain and multi-domain training settings, demonstrate competitive performance and support the effectiveness of coarse-to-fine adaptive diagnosis through targeted evidence acquisition and self-reflective refinement.The code is available at https://github.com/Xiaoyu-Tao/AnomaMind-TS.
items.author: Xiaoyu Tao, Yuchong Wu, Mingyue Cheng, Ze Guo, Min Wu

items.title: Computationally sufficient statistics for Ising models
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.12449v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Learning Gibbs distributions using only sufficient statistics has long been recognized as a computationally hard problem. On the other hand, computationally efficient algorithms for learning Gibbs distributions rely on access to full sample configurations generated from the model. For many systems of interest that arise in physical contexts, expecting a full sample to be observed is not practical, and hence it is important to look for computationally efficient methods that solve the learning problem with access to only a limited set of statistics. We examine the trade-offs between the power of computation and observation within this scenario, employing the Ising model as a paradigmatic example. We show that the couplings of the model can be learned to a desired accuracy from statistics whose order grows linearly with the $\ell_1$ width of the model and only logarithmically with the inverse of the accuracy. In particular, for a fixed accuracy, the required order is proportional to the width. This allows us to infer the model's structure, using statistics whose order grows logarithmically with the inverse of the weakest coupling, and also to learn its magnetic fields. When the width and the accuracy are fixed, the running time is polynomial in the number of variables. We also discuss a setting where prior information about structure of the model is available and show that the learning problem can be solved efficiently with even more limited observational power.
items.author: Abhijith Jayakumar, Shreya Shukla, Marc Vuffray, Andrey Y. Lokhov, Sidhant Misra

items.title: Amortized Molecular Optimization via Group Relative Policy Optimization
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.12162v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In structurally constrained molecular optimization, state-of-the-art methods treat every new input structure as a separate instance, restarting an expensive oracle-driven search from scratch and scaling poorly to settings with many starting structures or expensive oracles. While amortized approaches that learn a transferable policy could in principle remove this bottleneck, existing methods struggle to generalize to diverse structural constraints at inference time. We present AMORTIX, a Graph Transformer model that natively supports such constraints, optimizing molecular structures in a single rollout with zero inference-time oracle calls. A central challenge for amortized training in this domain is that optimization difficulty varies drastically across starting structures. We address this by centering rewards within groups of completions that share the same starting structure. We evaluate on goal-directed scaffold decoration, including single- and multi-target kinase inhibitor design, and on a few-shot prodrug case study. AMORTIX outperforms both amortized baselines and search-based instance optimizers on kinase scaffold decoration, and ablations across 23 objectives show that group-relative centering improves over REINFORCE and PPO and is substantially more consistent across scaffold splits. The prodrug case study further demonstrates transfer of learned modification rules to unseen drug structures.
items.author: Muhammad bin Javaid, Hasham Hussain, Ashima Khanna-Reiter, Berke Ki\c{s}in, Jonathan Pirnay, Alexander Mitsos, Dominik G. Grimm, Martin Grohe

items.title: Improved state mixing in higher-order and block diagonal linear recurrent networks
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.12021v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Linear recurrent networks (LRNNs) and linear state space models (SSMs) promise computational and memory efficiency on sequence modeling tasks, yet their diagonal state transitions limit expressivity. Dense and/or nonlinear architectures (e.g., LSTMs) on the other hand are provably more expressive, but computationally costly. Here, we explore how expressivity in LRNNs can be increased via richer state mixing across time and channels while maintaining competitive efficiency. Specifically, we introduce two structured LRNN architectures: (i) Higher-order Linear Recurrent Units (H-LRU), which generalize recurrences to arbitrary order, mixing multiple past states, and (ii) Block-Diagonal LRUs (BD-LRU), which enable dense intra-block channel mixing. To ensure stable training, we introduce a selective gate normalization scheme that allows for scalable window and block sizes. To maintain efficiency, we implement block-diagonal parallel scans in PyTorch and Triton that keep the throughput competitive with diagonal LRNNs for moderate orders (H-LRU) and block sizes (BD-LRU). Consistent with prior theoretical studies on the limitations of diagonal models, we empirically demonstrate that our architectures benefit from the increased expressivity of structured state mixing, on synthetic sequence modeling and on language modeling tasks that require tracking structure. Our results show that the structure of state mixing is a critical driver of performance in LRNNs, offering a practical pathway to closing the efficiency-expressivity gap in linear sequence models.
items.author: Igor Dubinin, Antonio Orvieto, Felix Effenberger

items.title: MUSE: Multi-Tenant Model Serving With Seamless Model Updates
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.11776v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In binary classification systems, decision thresholds translate model scores into actions. Choosing suitable thresholds relies on the specific distribution of the underlying model scores but also on the specific business decisions of each client using that model. However, retraining models inevitably shifts score distributions, invalidating existing thresholds. In multi-tenant Score-as-a-Service environments, where decision boundaries reside in client-managed infrastructure, this creates a severe bottleneck: recalibration requires coordinating threshold updates across hundreds of clients, consuming excessive human hours and leading to model stagnation. We introduce MUSE, a model serving framework that enables seamless model updates by decoupling model scores from client decision boundaries. Designed for multi-tenancy, MUSE optimizes infrastructure re-use by sharing models via dynamic intent-based routing, combined with a two-level score transformation that maps model outputs to a stable, reference distribution. Deployed at scale by Feedzai, MUSE processes over a thousand events per second, and over 55 billion events in the last 12 months, across several dozens of tenants, while maintaining high-availability and low-latency guarantees. By reducing model lead time from weeks to minutes, MUSE promotes model resilience against shifting attacks, saving millions of dollars in fraud losses and operational costs.
items.author: Cl\'audio Correia, Alberto E. A. Ferreira, Lucas Martins, Miguel P. Bento, Sofia Guerreiro, Ricardo Ribeiro Pereira, Ana Sofia Gomes, Jacopo Bono, Hugo Ferreira, Pedro Bizarro

items.title: Causal Multi-Task Demand Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.09969v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study multi-task demand learning for retail pricing, where firms seek to estimate heterogeneous linear price-response functions across many decision contexts. Each context has rich covariates but limited price variation, motivating transfer across tasks. However, such transfer is complicated by endogeneity: prices may be arbitrarily correlated with unobserved task-level demand determinants.
  We propose a meta-learning framework that identifies the conditional mean of task-specific causal demand parameters despite this confounding, provided each task contains at least two distinct, locally exogenous price points. The key is to carefully design the information available to the learner. We condition on the full price history to address cross-task confounding, but withhold the demand outcomes associated with two locally exogenous price points to preserve identifiability. These withheld outcomes provide supervision through a randomized query.
  We establish that this information design is maximally uniformly valid for the squared-loss objective: any refinement of the conditioning set that reveals information about the withheld outcomes or the query index admits a data-generating process under which the objective no longer identifies the conditional mean causal target. Synthetic experiments demonstrate improved estimation of causal demand parameters under strong confounding, while retail experiments show improved held-out demand prediction relative to standard transfer-learning baselines.
items.author: Varun Gupta, Vijay Kamble

items.title: Laplacian Heads Improve Transformers by Smoothing Token Representations
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.09297v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Transformers update token representations through multi-head attention and residual connections: $X \leftarrow X + \sum_{i} P^{(i)}\text{Norm}(X)W_{V_i}W_{o_i}$, where $P^{(i)}$ is the softmax probability matrix in head $i$. We propose replacing some $P^{(i)}$'s with $I - P^{(i)}$, giving $X \leftarrow X + \sum_{i \in \mathcal{A}} P^{(i)}\text{Norm}(X)W_{V_i}W_{o_i} + \sum_{i \in \mathcal{L}} (I - P^{(i)})\text{Norm}(X)W_{V_i}W_{o_i}$. We call heads that use $I - P^{(i)}$ Laplacian heads. Our proposal has two motivations. First, it allows attention heads to update the mean of token representations, while Laplacian heads can directly control within-sequence variance. Second, if tokens are viewed as nodes in a graph with normalized edge weights $P^{(i)}$, then $I - P^{(i)}$ is a graph Laplacian operator, and the update can be interpreted as one step of heat diffusion on the graph. We show that this simple modification improves performance across supervised learning, causal language modeling, and vision self-supervised learning tasks. To investigate why, we examine the token representations learned with and without Laplacian heads. In supervised learning, Laplacian heads collapse token representations within the same sequence and align the sequence means with the geometry of Neural Collapse. In language modeling, they increase the separability of token representations that share the same next-token prediction. In vision self-supervised learning, they produce token representations whose top principal components better capture segmentation structure. Across modalities, they also lead to faster-decaying spectra, indicating stronger token smoothing. Overall, our findings challenge the prevailing view that token oversmoothing is inherently harmful, showing instead that certain forms of smoothing can be beneficial.
items.author: Yuchong Zhang, Vardan Papyan

items.title: Reusable Conditional Resampling via Flow Matching for Constraint-Based Causal Discovery
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.08315v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Constraint-based causal discovery requires many conditional independence (CI) tests. Generative CI tests are attractive in nonlinear and high-dimensional settings because they can model complex conditional distributions, but often suffer from high per-test costs and limited reusability across query-dependent conditional resampling tasks in graph search. We propose a generative nonlinear CI testing and graph search framework for PC-style causal discovery. We introduce Langevin-RePaint for conditional imputation. Building on Langevin-RePaint and joint flow matching modeling, we propose the Flow Matching based Conditional Independence Test (FMCIT), which reformulates generative CI testing from query-specific conditional modeling into a reusable conditional resampling framework. We establish theoretical guarantees for FMCIT's type-I error control. FMCIT reuses a single trained generative model to generate randomized copies throughout graph search. We then introduce GPC-FMCIT, which embeds FMCIT into a guided PC pipeline with screening, guidance, refinement, and orientation. By using low-cost screening to shrink the search space, constructing edge-specific candidate conditioning sets from local graph structure, and invoking FMCIT only in a budget-controlled refinement stage, GPC-FMCIT reduces both the deployment cost of individual nonlinear CI queries and the overall query complexity. On synthetic nonlinear structural equation models, GPC-FMCIT improves CPDAG recovery over PC-stable baselines and requires far fewer FMCIT queries than direct FMCIT-based PC search, and on hESC gene-expression data it yields smaller graphs than PC/FisherZ in a descriptive comparison. Overall, our results suggest that, through the joint design of reusable conditional resampling and controlled graph search, generative nonlinear CI testing can become a practical component of PC-style causal discovery.
items.author: Shunyu Zhao, Yanfeng Yang, Shuai Li, Kenji Fukumizu

items.title: Efficient Adaptive Data Analysis over Dense Distributions
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.07732v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Modern data workflows are inherently adaptive, repeatedly querying the same dataset to refine and validate sequential decisions, but such adaptivity can lead to overfitting and invalid statistical inference. Adaptive Data Analysis (ADA) mechanisms address this challenge; however, there is a fundamental tension between computational efficiency and sample complexity. For $T$ rounds of adaptive analysis, computationally efficient algorithms typically incur suboptimal $O(\sqrt{T})$ sample complexity, whereas for arbitrary distributions, algorithms with $O(\log T)$ sample complexity are computationally intractable under standard cryptographic assumptions. In this work, we shed light on this trade-off by identifying a natural class of data distributions under which both computational efficiency and logarithmic sample complexity in $T$ are achievable. We propose a computationally efficient ADA mechanism that attains $O(\log T)$ sample complexity, optimal in its dependence on $T$, when the data distribution is dense with respect to a known prior. This setting includes, in particular, feature-label data distributions arising in distribution-specific learning. As a consequence, our mechanism also yields a sample-efficient (i.e., $O(\log T)$ samples) statistical query oracle in the distribution-specific setting. Moreover, although our algorithm is not based on differential privacy, it satisfies a relaxed privacy notion known as Predicate Singling Out (PSO) security (Cohen and Nissim 2020) whenever the number of its possible update transcripts is polynomial in the sample size. Our results thus reveal an inherent connection between adaptive data analysis and privacy beyond differential privacy.
items.author: Joon Suk Huh

items.title: Closed-Form Implicit Neural Representations
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.07603v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Training implicit neural representations (INRs) to capture fine-scale details typically relies on iterative backpropagation and is often hindered by spectral bias when the target exhibits highly non-uniform frequency content. We propose ELM-INR, a backpropagation-free INR that decomposes the domain into overlapping subdomains and fits each local problem using an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) in closed form, replacing iterative optimization with stable linear least-squares solutions. This design yields fast and numerically robust reconstruction by combining local predictors through a partition of unity. To understand where approximation becomes difficult under fixed local capacity, we analyze the method from a spectral Barron norm perspective, which reveals that global reconstruction error is dominated by regions with high spectral complexity. Building on this insight, we introduce BEAM, an adaptive mesh refinement strategy that balances spectral complexity across subdomains to improve reconstruction quality in capacity-constrained regimes.
items.author: Woojin Cho, Junghwan Park

items.title: CORP: Closed-Form One-shot Representation-Preserving Structured Pruning
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.05243v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Transformers achieve strong accuracy but incur high compute and memory cost. Structured pruning reduces inference cost, but most methods rely on retraining or multi-stage optimization, which limits post-training deployment. We propose CORP, a closed-form one-shot structured pruning method that removes MLP dimensions and attention substructures using only unlabeled calibration data without gradients or fine-tuning. CORP formulates structured pruning as a representation recovery problem. It models removed components as affine functions of retained components and derives closed-form ridge regression solutions that fold compensation into model weights. This minimizes a layer-local affine/logit reconstruction objective under the calibration distribution. Experiments on ImageNet with DeiT reveal strong redundancy in both MLP and attention representations. With CORP, models retain high accuracy under aggressive sparsity. On DeiT-Huge, CORP achieves 83.24% Top-1 accuracy after pruning 50% of both MLP and attention structures.
items.author: Boxiang Zhang, Baijian Yang

items.title: Disentangled Representation Learning via Flow Matching
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.05214v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Disentangled representation learning aims to capture the underlying explanatory factors of observed data, enabling a principled understanding of the data-generating process. Recent advances in generative modeling have introduced new paradigms for learning such representations. However, existing diffusion-based methods encourage factor independence via inductive biases, yet frequently lack strong semantic alignment. In this work, we propose a flow matching-based framework for disentangled representation learning, which casts disentanglement as learning factor-conditioned flows in a compact latent space. To enforce explicit semantic alignment, we introduce a non-overlap (orthogonality) regularizer that suppresses cross-factor interference and reduces information leakage between factors. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over representative baselines, yielding higher disentanglement scores as well as improved controllability and sample fidelity.
items.author: Jinjin Chi, Taoping Liu, Mengtao Yin, Ximing Li, Yongcheng Jing, Jialie Shen, Leszek Rutkowski, Dacheng Tao

items.title: Decoupling Time and Risk: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning with General Discounting
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.04131v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Distributional reinforcement learning (RL) is a powerful framework increasingly adopted in safety-critical domains for its ability to optimize risk-sensitive objectives. However, the role of the discount factor is often overlooked, as it is typically treated as a fixed parameter of the Markov decision process or tunable hyperparameter, with little consideration of its effect on the learned policy. In the literature, it is well-known that the discounting function plays a major role in characterizing time preferences of an agent, which an exponential discount factor cannot fully capture. Building on this insight, we propose a novel framework that supports flexible discounting of future rewards and optimization of risk measures in distributional RL. We provide a technical analysis of the optimality of our algorithms, show that our multi-horizon extension fixes issues raised with existing methodologies, and validate the robustness of our methods through extensive experiments. Our results highlight that discounting is a cornerstone in decision-making problems for capturing more expressive temporal and risk preferences profiles, with potential implications for real-world safety-critical applications.
items.author: Mehrdad Moghimi, Anthony Coache, Hyejin Ku

items.title: Partition Tree: Conditional Density Estimation over General Outcome Spaces
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.04042v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose Partition Tree, a tree-based framework for conditional density estimation over general outcome spaces that supports both continuous and categorical variables within a unified formulation. Our approach models conditional distributions as piecewise-constant densities on data-adaptive partitions and learns trees by greedily minimizing a surrogate for conditional log-loss. This yields a scalable alternative to existing probabilistic trees that does not make parametric assumptions about the target distribution. We further introduce Partition Forest, an ensemble extension obtained by averaging conditional densities. Empirically, we demonstrate improved probabilistic prediction over CART-style trees and competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art probabilistic tree methods and Random Forests.
items.author: Felipe Angelim, Alessandro Leite

items.title: NPCNet: Navigator-Driven Pseudo Text for Deep Clustering of Early Sepsis Phenotyping
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.03562v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Sepsis is a heterogeneous syndrome. Identifying clinically distinct phenotypes may enable more precise treatment strategies. In recent years, many researchers have applied clustering algorithms to sepsis patients. However, many existing approaches require aggregating or imputing temporal Electronic Health Records (EHRs), which can limit the model's ability to capture disease progression. Furthermore, existing clustering processes seldom incorporate domain-driven constraints, often resulting in phenotypes that lack clear clinical distinction. We propose a novel clustering network, NPCNet, that comprises a text embedding generator, a clustering operator, and a target navigator. We first transformed EHRs into pseudo texts by discretizing continuous clinical measurements and integrated them with static variables to construct the embeddings. The target navigator then infused clinical knowledge into the embeddings through auxiliary tasks, constraining clustering results to better align sepsis phenotypes with clinical significance. Finally, the clustering operator employed an iterative refinement mechanism to jointly optimize phenotype centroids and patient representations under domain-driven constraints. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrated that NPCNet achieved superior performance on both internal clustering and clinical metrics. We identify four distinct sepsis phenotypes with divergent SOFA trajectories. Notably, although {\alpha} and {\delta} exhibit similarly severe conditions initially, NPCNet distinguishes patients likely to improve ({\alpha}) from those at risk of deterioration ({\delta}). Furthermore, treatment effect analysis suggests that early vasopressor administration may be associated with improved outcomes in the {\alpha}, \{beta}, and {\delta} phenotypes. These findings highlight NPCNet's potential for phenotype-specific treatment strategies.
items.author: Pi-Ju Tsai, Charkkri Limbud, Kuan-Fu Chen, Yi-Ju Tseng

items.title: Soft-Radial Projection for Constrained End-to-End Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.03461v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Constrained end-to-end learning trains neural networks whose outputs must satisfy feasibility constraints, such as resource, budget, or operational limits. While projection and optimization layers guarantee constraint satisfaction, boundary-based projections can introduce unfavorable optimization geometry: regions of the unconstrained output space are mapped to the same active face of the feasible set. This makes the resulting map locally rank-deficient, suppressing gradients in constrained directions and potentially impairing optimization - a bottleneck known as gradient saturation. We propose Soft-Radial Projection (SRP), a differentiable reparameterization layer that maps unconstrained network outputs into the relative interior of a convex feasible set by smoothly rescaling rays from a strictly feasible anchor point. Unlike hard radial or orthogonal projections, the resulting map is one-to-one and has a full-rank Jacobian almost everywhere, while guaranteeing strict feasibility. We prove that constrained networks equipped with SRP retain universal approximation guarantees. For polytopes and balls, the layer admits a closed-form forward pass, while for general convex sets, the ray-boundary intersection reduces to a one-dimensional search. Experiments on decision-focused learning benchmarks demonstrate strong solution quality at low computational cost, with particularly favorable results in portfolio optimization and substantially lower inference latency than differentiable optimization layers in the evaluated settings.
items.author: Philipp J. Schneider, Daniel Kuhn

items.title: A Reduction from Delayed to Immediate Feedback for Online Convex Optimization with Improved Guarantees
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.02634v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This paper develops a reduction-based framework for online learning with delayed feedback that recovers and improves upon existing results for first-order and bandit convex optimization. We introduce a continuous-time model that enables an observation-centric rather than prediction-centric analysis. Under this model, regret decomposes into a delay-independent learning term and a delay-induced drift term, yielding a delay-adaptive reduction that converts any online linear optimization algorithm into one that handles round-dependent delays. For bandit convex optimization, we significantly improve existing regret bounds, with delay-dependent terms matching optimal first-order rates. For first-order feedback, we recover optimal regret bounds via a simpler, unified analysis.
  Quantitatively, for bandit convex optimization we obtain $O(\sqrt{d_{\text{tot}}} + T^{\frac{3}{4}}\sqrt{k})$ regret, improving the delay-dependent term from $O(\min\{\sqrt{T d_{\text{max}}},(Td_{\text{tot}})^{\frac{1}{3}}\})$ in prior work to $O(\sqrt{d_{\text{tot}}})$. Here, $k$, $T$, $d_{\text{max}}$, and $d_{\text{tot}}$ denote the dimension, time horizon, maximum and total delay, respectively. Under strong convexity, we achieve $O(\min\{\sigma_{\text{max}} \ln T, \sqrt{d_{\text{tot}}}\} + (T^2\ln T)^{\frac{1}{3}} {k}^{\frac{2}{3}})$, improving the delay-dependent term from $O(d_{\text{max}} \ln T)$ to $O(\min\{\sigma_{\text{max}} \ln T, \sqrt{d_{\text{tot}}}\})$, where $\sigma_{\text{max}}$ denotes the maximum number of outstanding observations and may be considerably smaller than $d_{\text{max}}$.
items.author: Alexander Ryabchenko, Idan Attias, Daniel M. Roy

items.title: Self-Rewarding Sequential Monte Carlo for Masked Diffusion Language Models
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.01849v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: This work presents self-rewarding sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), an inference-time scaling algorithm enabling effective sampling of masked diffusion language models (MDLMs). Our algorithm stems from the observation that most existing MDLMs rely on a confidence-based sampling strategy, where only tokens with the highest prediction confidence are preserved at each step. This restricts the generation to a noise-sensitive, greedy decoding paradigm, resulting in an inevitable collapse in the diversity of possible paths. We address this problem by launching multiple interacting diffusion processes in parallel, referred to as particles, for trajectory exploration. Importantly, we introduce the trajectory-level confidence as a self-rewarding signal for assigning particle importance weights. During sampling, particles are iteratively weighted and resampled to systematically steer generation towards globally confident, high-quality samples. Our self-rewarding SMC is verified on various masked diffusion language models and benchmarks, achieving significant improvement without extra training or reward guidance, while effectively converting parallel inference capacity into improved sampling quality. Our code is available at https://github.com/Algolzw/self-rewarding-smc.
items.author: Ziwei Luo, Ziqi Jin, Lei Wang, Lidong Bing, Thomas B. Sch\"on

items.title: COMET: Codebook-based Online-adaptive Multi-scale Embedding for Time-series Anomaly Detection
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.01635v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Multivariate time-series anomaly detection aims to identify abnormal temporal patterns in complex real-world systems. However, robust unsupervised time-series anomaly detection remains challenging because anomalies can manifest over different temporal ranges and emerge from interactions among variables, while distribution shifts can cause normal patterns to drift over time. To address these challenges, we propose Codebook-based Online-adaptive Multi-scale Embedding for Time-series anomaly detection (COMET), a unified framework with three tightly coupled components. First, Multi-scale Patch Encoder learns correlation-aware patch embeddings by combining variable-specific temporal dynamics with shared inter-variable structure across multiple patch scales. Second, Vector-Quantized Coreset quantizes these embeddings into representative normal prototypes, which are used to detect anomalies through a dual score combining quantization error and density-aware memory distance. Third, Online Codebook Adaptation leverages the same codebook structure to identify reliable normal samples from training-activated codebook entries, and then updates the prototypes through contrastive learning at inference time. Experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that COMET achieves the best performance on 39 out of 45 evaluation metrics compared to seven baselines, showing robust performance across diverse evaluation protocols.
items.author: Jinwoo Park, Hyeongwon Kang, Seung Hun Han, Pilsung Kang

items.title: Understanding What TRAK Gets Right and Wrong: A Theory of Data Attribution
items.summary:
arXiv:2602.01312v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Data attribution, which traces a model's prediction back to specific training data, is an important tool for interpreting sophisticated AI models. The widely used TRAK algorithm addresses this challenge by first approximating the underlying model with a kernel machine and then leveraging techniques developed for approximating the leave-one-out (ALO) risk. Despite its strong empirical performance, the theoretical conditions under which TRAK approximations are accurate, as well as the regimes in which they break down, remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we provide a theoretical analysis of the TRAK algorithm, characterizing its performance and quantifying the errors introduced by the approximations on which the method relies. We show that although the approximations can incur significant errors, TRAK preserves the separation between highly influential and weakly influential data points. We corroborate our theoretical results through extensive simulations and empirical studies.
items.author: Han Tong, Haolin Zou, Shubhangi Ghosh, Arian Maleki

items.title: TriSpec: Ternary Speculative Decoding via Lightweight Proxy Verification
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.23180v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Inference efficiency in Large Language Models (LLMs) is fundamentally limited by their serial, autoregressive generation, especially as reasoning becomes a key capability and response sequences grow longer. Speculative decoding (SD) offers a powerful solution, providing significant speed-ups through its lightweight drafting and parallel verification mechanism. While existing work has nearly saturated improvements in draft effectiveness and efficiency, this paper advances SD from a new yet critical perspective: the verification cost. We propose TriSpec, a novel ternary SD framework that, at its core, introduces a lightweight proxy to significantly reduce computational cost by approving easily verifiable draft sequences and engaging the full target model only when encountering uncertain tokens. TriSpec can be integrated with state-of-the-art SD methods like EAGLE-3 to further reduce verification costs, achieving greater acceleration. Extensive experiments on the Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen/LLaMA families show that TriSpec achieves up to 35% speedup over standard SD, with up to 50% fewer target model invocations while maintaining comparable accuracy.
items.author: Haoyun Jiang, Junqi He, Feng Hong, Xinlong Yang, Jianwei Zhang, Zhengyang Zhuge, Zheng Li, Xiaofeng Cao, Zhiyong Chen, Bo Han, Junyang Lin, Jiangchao Yao

items.title: JURIST: Training Small Data-Reweighted Reasoning Judges for Test-Time Scaling in Code Generation
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.22230v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Best-of-N selection for code generation is only as good as the judge that picks among the candidates, and the judges accurate enough for this role are costly frontier LLMs. A small judge can be trained on abundant earlier data labeled by unit tests, but it is deployed on newer problems: the earlier problems are easier and teach it little, their tasks differ, and their candidates come from weaker policies, while data close to deployment are scarce. We present JURIST, a 1.7B reasoning judge that uses a small meta set close to deployment to learn how much each earlier training sample should count. In our experiments, we find that training on the meta set alone, or adding it to the training data, does not help, while using it to weight the earlier data through a bi-level objective adds 3.9 Hard points over adding it to the training data. On LiveCodeBench, JURIST reaches 84.7% Overall and matches Claude Sonnet 4.6 on Hard problems (73.8%) at 463x lower cost; on BigCodeBench, it surpasses all test-time scaling baselines (35.9%). Abundant earlier data, guided by a small deployment-aligned meta set, can thus train a compact judge that selects accurately at low cost.
items.author: Peijia Qin, Ruiyi Zhang, Qi Cao, Pengtao Xie

items.title: Sampling-Free Privacy Accounting for Matrix Mechanisms under Random Allocation
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.21636v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study privacy amplification for differentially private model training with matrix factorization under random allocation (also known as the balls-in-bins model). Recent work by Choquette-Choo et al. (2025) proposes a sampling-based Monte Carlo approach to compute amplification parameters in this setting. However, their guarantees either only hold with some high probability or require random abstention by the mechanism. Furthermore, the required number of samples for ensuring $(\epsilon,\delta)$-DP is inversely proportional to $\delta$. In contrast, we develop sampling-free bounds based on R\'enyi divergence and conditional composition. The former is facilitated by a dynamic programming formulation to efficiently compute the bounds. The latter complements it by offering stronger privacy guarantees for small $\epsilon$, where R\'enyi divergence bounds inherently lead to an over-approximation. Our framework applies to arbitrary banded and non-banded matrices. Through numerical comparisons, we demonstrate the efficacy of our approach across a broad range of matrix mechanisms used in research and practice.
items.author: Jan Schuchardt, Nikita Kalinin

items.title: Monotone Optimisation with Learned Projections
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.20983v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Optimisation algorithms typically assume oracle access to objectives and constraints, yet in many applications these functions are available only through data. To recover them, a common approach learns a surrogate for each function and optimises over it, but this can be unnecessarily expensive and may fail to preserve the structure required by the optimisation algorithm. We study this problem for monotone optimisation, a class of non-convex problems which can be solved globally using the Polyblock Outer Approximation (POA) algorithm. Our key observation is that POA does not require the constraint functions themselves, but only a scalar quantity we call the radial inverse. Learning this quantity directly replaces POA's inner bisection loop over a learned constraint with a single radial inverse evaluation. We characterise exactly which maps arise as radial inverses of monotone constraints, and relate their approximation error to perturbations of the feasible set and optimal objective value. Building on these results, we introduce Homogeneous-Monotone Radial Inverse (HM-RI) networks, structured min-max models that enforce the monotonicity and positive-homogeneity of radial inverses by construction. Across synthetic monotone optimisation problems and a cellular transmit-power application, HM-RI improves solution quality over direct constraint surrogates and local optimisation baselines by up to 58.6 percentage points relative to the Oracle reference objective, while achieving a 3.0-4.7x speed-up over bisection-based POA with learned constraint surrogates, with the largest solution-quality gains occurring in data-limited and piecewise-constant settings.
items.author: Ahmed Rashwan, Keith Briggs, Chris Budd, Lisa Kreusser

items.title: Spectral Ghost in Representation Learning: A Unified View from Component Analysis to Self-Supervised Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.20154v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) extracts representations from massive unlabeled data that transfer to a variety of downstream tasks. Its empirical success has produced a dizzying array of objectives and procedures, yet a clear understanding of what representation is desired, and why these seemingly different methods work, is still missing. In this paper, we develop a unified spectral framework for representation learning. We first show that a representation is sufficient for arbitrary downstream prediction with a linear head if it spans the spectral decomposition of the pointwise mutual information, which can be extracted purely from unlabeled data. This view organizes representation learning along two axes, the parametrization of the spectral representation (linear, energy-based, denoising, nonlinear, latent-variable, and multi-modal) and the learning objective for fitting it, under which a broad range of existing methods, including SimCLR, MoCo, BYOL, Barlow Twins, VICReg, DINO, MAE, JEPA, BERT, GPT, and CLIP, as well as classic PCA, CCA, Laplacian eigenmaps, LLE, and SNE, are recovered as particular combinations. The framework also clarifies optimization behaviors: the batch-size requirement is determined by whether the objective is unbiased, a consistent surrogate, or biased, rather than by contrastive vs. non-contrastive losses. Finally, the framework inspires new scalable algorithms and extends spectral representations to causal inference and reinforcement learning.
items.author: Bo Dai, Na Li, Dale Schuurmans

items.title: The Trajectory Alignment Coefficient in Two Acts: From Reward Tuning to Reward Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.16906v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The success of RL is fundamentally tied to having a reward function that accurately reflects the task objective. Yet, designing reward functions is time-consuming and prone to misspecification. To address this, our first goal is to understand how to support RL practitioners in specifying reward functions. We leverage the Trajectory Alignment Coefficient (TAC), a metric that evaluates how closely a reward function's induced preferences match those of a domain expert. To test whether TAC provides meaningful support, we evaluated its impact in a user study where practitioners designed reward functions for Lunar Lander. We found that iterative TAC feedback allowed participants to design more performant reward functions while reporting lower cognitive workload than unguided reward design. However, the study also underscored that manual reward design, even with TAC, remains labor-intensive. This motivated our second goal: to learn a reward model that maximizes TAC directly. Specifically, we propose Soft-TAC, a differentiable approximation of TAC that can be used as a loss function to train reward models from human preferences. Our theoretical analysis guarantees that under Soft-TAC optimization: (1) the optimal reward function belongs exclusively to the set of human-aligned reward functions, and (2) this optimal reward remains invariant whether trained on clean or noisy preference data. Empirically, we first evaluate reward models trained with Soft-TAC across three robotic tasks, demonstrating that they consistently match or outperform those trained with the Cross-Entropy loss. Next, we evaluate Soft-TAC in the GT7 driving simulator, and find that Soft-TAC-trained reward models more successfully capture preference-specific driving styles. Ultimately, this work demonstrates that TAC can serve as both a practical tool for guiding reward design and a reward learning objective in complex domains.
items.author: Calarina Muslimani, Yunshu Du, Kenta Kawamoto, Kaushik Subramanian, Peter Stone, Peter Wurman

items.title: Stagewise Reinforcement Learning and the Geometry of the Regret Landscape
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.07524v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Singular learning theory characterizes Bayesian learning as an evolving tradeoff between accuracy and complexity, with transitions between qualitatively different solutions as sample size increases. We extend this theory to reinforcement learning, proving that the concentration of a generalized posterior over policies is governed by the local learning coefficient (LLC), an invariant of the geometry of the regret function. This theory predicts that deep reinforcement learning with SGD should proceed from simple policies with high regret to complex policies with low regret. We verify this prediction empirically in a gridworld environment exhibiting stagewise policy development: phase transitions over training manifest as "opposing staircases" where regret decreases sharply while the LLC increases.
items.author: Chris Elliott, Einar Urdshals, David Quarel, Matthew Farrugia-Roberts, Daniel Murfet

items.title: Mosaic: Unlocking Over 30$\times$ Context Length for Diffusion LLMs Inference via Global Memory Planning and Dynamic Peak Taming
items.summary:
arXiv:2601.06562v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Diffusion-based large language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive models, leveraging simultaneous denoising to enable global planning and iterative refinement. These properties make dLLMs attractive for long-context generation. However, deploying dLLMs faces a prohibitive memory barrier, as existing inference systems are inefficient for the diffusion paradigm. We observe that current inference systems are misaligned with dLLMs. Unlike autoregressive models, whose memory footprint is dominated by the KV-Cache, dLLMs are bottlenecked by transient activations rematerialized per step. Moreover, generic memory reuse mechanisms lack the global visibility to handle dynamic memory peaks of dLLMs, which alternate between logits and feed-forward networks. To address these challenges, we present Mosaic, a memory-efficient inference system that shifts dLLM execution from local, static management to a global, dynamic paradigm. Mosaic integrates (i) a mask-only logits kernel eliminating redundant activation materialization, (ii) a lazy chunking optimizer using online heuristics to tame dynamic memory peaks, and (iii) a global memory manager leveraging virtual addressing to mitigate memory fragmentation. Evaluations show that Mosaic reduces the memory peak-to-average ratio by 2.71$\times$ on average and increases the maximum inference sequence length on identical hardware by 15.30-32.34$\times$. Crucially, Mosaic is training-free and preserves exact model outputs, while reducing end-to-end latency by 2.5%-55.4%. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/flashserve/Mosaic.
items.author: Liang Zheng, Bowen Shi, Yitao Hu, Jiawei Zhang, Ruofan Li, Guotao Yang, Zhixin Zhao, Zhengchao Wang, Sheng Chen, Wenxin Li, Dezhi Ran, Tao Xie, Keqiu Li

items.title: gHAWK: Local and Global Structure Encoding for Scalable Training of Graph Neural Networks on Knowledge Graphs
items.summary:
arXiv:2512.08274v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) are a rich source of structured data, and graph neural networks (GNNs) are the dominant tool for learning over them. However, existing message-passing GNNs struggle to scale to large KGs because they rely on the iterative message passing process to learn graph structure. This process is inefficient, especially under mini-batch training, where a node sees only a partial view of its neighborhood. In this paper, we address this problem and present gHAWK, a novel and scalable GNN training framework for large KGs. The key idea is to precompute structural features for each node that capture its local and global structure before GNN training even begins. Specifically, gHAWK introduces a preprocessing step that computes: (a)~Bloom filters to compactly encode local neighborhood structure, and (b)~TransE embeddings to represent each node's global position in the graph. These features are then fused with any domain-specific features (e.g., text embeddings), producing a node feature vector that can be used with any GNN backbone. Equipped with these structural priors, the GNN no longer needs to rediscover graph structure, significantly improving convergence and model accuracy with little memory overhead. Extensive experiments on large datasets from the Open Graph Benchmark demonstrate that gHAWK improves accuracy on both node property prediction and link prediction tasks. Remarkably, gHAWK enables simple GNNs to match or exceed more complex relation-aware ones, suggesting that careful preprocessing can substitute for architectural complexity in KG learning.
items.author: Humera Sabir, Fatima Farooq, Ashraf Aboulnaga

items.title: LeMat-GenBench: A Unified Evaluation Framework for Crystal Generative Models
items.summary:
arXiv:2512.04562v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Generative machine learning (ML) models hold great promise for accelerating materials discovery through the inverse design of inorganic crystals, enabling an unprecedented exploration of chemical space. Yet, the lack of standardized evaluation frameworks makes it challenging to evaluate, compare, and further develop these ML models meaningfully. In this work, we introduce LeMat-GenBench, a unified benchmark for generative models of crystalline materials, supported by a set of evaluation metrics designed to better inform model development and downstream applications. We release both an open-source evaluation suite and a public leaderboard on Hugging Face, and benchmark 12 recent generative models. Results reveal that an increase in stability is accompanied by lower novelty and diversity on average, with no model excelling across all dimensions. Altogether, LeMat-GenBench establishes a reproducible and extensible foundation for fair model comparison and aims to guide the development of more reliable, discovery-oriented generative models for crystalline materials.
items.author: Siddharth Betala, Samuel P. Gleason, Ali Ramlaoui, Andy Xu, Georgia Channing, Daniel Levy, Cl\'ementine Fourrier, Nikita Kazeev, Chaitanya K. Joshi, S\'ekou-Oumar Kaba, F\'elix Therrien, Alex Hernandez-Garcia, Roc\'io Mercado, N. M. Anoop Krishnan, Alexandre Duval

items.title: GLOBE: Accurate Surrogates for Boundary-Driven PDEs via Domain-Inspired Architectures and Equivariance
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.15856v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce GLOBE, a nonlinear neural surrogate for boundary-driven, homogeneous, weakly nonlinear PDEs that draws inductive bias from boundary-element methods and equivariant ML, representing solutions as superpositions of learnable Green's-function-like kernels evaluated from boundary faces to targets. The architecture is translation-, rotation-, and parity-equivariant; discretization-invariant; and units-invariant via rigorous nondimensionalization. On AirFRANS (steady incompressible RANS over NACA airfoils), a compact ~117k-parameter GLOBE model has lower mean-squared error than published values for the strongest reported ML surrogates on both the interpolation and low-data splits, in single-run comparisons under the released AirFRANS normalization. The model evaluates fields at arbitrary points, handles non-watertight meshes, and generalizes under Reynolds number and angle-of-attack distribution shifts. We further introduce a hierarchical Barnes-Hut acceleration that exploits the kernel's far-field decay to reduce evaluation cost from quadratic to near-linear in the number of boundary elements, with a tunable opening angle that recovers exact dense evaluation in the zero-angle limit. Quantitative validation focuses on 2D AirFRANS; on 3D DrivAerML cars, GLOBE predicts surface and volume fields on the full meshes, and we compare it with a matched Transolver baseline. Together, these results show that boundary-element-inspired inductive biases can substantially improve the accuracy of ML surrogates for boundary-driven PDEs while scaling to large 3D meshes.
items.author: Peter Sharpe

items.title: Private Sparse Sketches for Linear Regression
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.07365v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Sketching compresses a large dataset into a smaller summary, allowing regression on the sketch to approximate the full-data objective. A sketch released under differential privacy can be reused with any non-private regression solver, any number of times, without further privacy loss. We study private sparse sketches for $\ell_2$ and $\ell_1$ regression. We first prove lower bounds on the noise required by common sparse sketches for both problems when the sketching matrix is public. Since regression on a sketch can be solved without revealing the sketching matrix, we construct sketches whose randomness is kept secret. Hiding how individual records enter the sketch provides an additional source of privacy, allowing less noise for the same privacy guarantee. We prove differential privacy guarantees for both constructions, and experiments on real datasets show improved utility over public-sketch baselines.
items.author: Shrutimoy Das, Anirban Dasgupta

items.title: Diffusion LLMs are Natural Adversaries for any LLM
items.summary:
arXiv:2511.00203v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We introduce a novel framework that transforms the resource-intensive (adversarial) prompt optimization problem into an \emph{efficient, amortized inference task}. Our core insight is that pretrained, non-autoregressive generative LLMs, such as Diffusion LLMs, which model the joint distribution over prompt-response pairs, can serve as powerful surrogates for prompt search. This approach enables direct conditional generation of prompts, effectively replacing costly discrete optimization with a small number of parallelizable samples. We provide a probabilistic analysis demonstrating that under mild fidelity assumptions, only a few conditional samples are required to recover high-reward (harmful) prompts. Empirically, our method substantially outperforms prior attacks in both success rate and compute cost, producing low-perplexity, diverse jailbreaks that transfer to a wide range of black-box target models, including robustly trained and proprietary LLMs. Beyond adversarial prompting, our framework opens new directions for red teaming, automated prompt optimization, and leveraging emerging Flow- and Diffusion-based LLMs.
items.author: David L\"udke, Tom Wollschl\"ager, Paul Ungermann, Stephan G\"unnemann, Leo Schwinn

items.title: A Framework for Bounding Deterministic Risk with PAC-Bayes: Applications to Majority Votes
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.25569v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: PAC-Bayes is a popular and efficient framework for obtaining generalization guarantees in situations involving uncountable hypothesis spaces. Unfortunately, in its classical formulation, it only provides guarantees on the expected risk of a randomly sampled hypothesis. This requires stochastic predictions at test time, making PAC-Bayes unusable in many practical situations where a single deterministic hypothesis must be deployed. We propose a unified framework for extracting guarantees for a single hypothesis from PAC-Bayesian guarantees. We present a general derandomization framework, and derive from it a numerical bound for majority votes and for three different probability distributions over the posterior space. We study the empirical behaviour of our approach, showing that it consistently outperforms popular baselines in terms of generalization bounds for single classifiers (by up to a factor of 2), but sometimes requires a sacrifice in accuracy.
items.author: Benjamin Leblanc, Pascal Germain

items.title: Convergence Analysis of SGD under Expected Smoothness
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.20608v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is the workhorse of large-scale learning, yet classical analyses rely on assumptions that can be either too strong (bounded variance) or too coarse (uniform noise). The expected smoothness (ES) condition has emerged as a flexible alternative that ties the second moment of stochastic gradients to the objective value and the full gradient. This paper presents a self-contained convergence analysis of SGD under ES. We (i) refine ES with interpretations and sampling-dependent constants; (ii) derive bounds of the expectation of squared full gradient norm; and (iii) prove sublinear convergence rates with explicit residual errors for various step-size schedules. Furthermore, we empirically validate our theoretical framework by training a ResNet-18 model on the CIFAR-100 dataset. We uncover a two-phase dynamic in the gradient noise structure, transitioning from a suboptimality-dominated regime to a geometry-dominated regime. Our treatment unifies and extends recent theoretical threads in the literature.
items.author: Yuta Kawamoto, Hideaki Iiduka

items.title: Mamba Can Learn Low-Dimensional Targets In-Context via Test-Time Feature Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2510.12026v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Mamba, a recently proposed linear-time sequence model, has attracted significant attention for its computational efficiency and strong empirical performance. However, a rigorous theoretical understanding of its underlying mechanisms remains limited. In this work, we provide a theoretical analysis of Mamba's in-context learning (ICL) capability by focusing on tasks defined by low-dimensional nonlinear target functions. Specifically, we study in-context learning of a single-index model $y \approx g_*(\langle \boldsymbol{\beta}, \boldsymbol{x} \rangle)$, which depends on only a single relevant direction $\boldsymbol{\beta}$, referred to as feature. We prove that Mamba, pretrained by gradient-based methods, can achieve efficient ICL via test-time feature learning, extracting the relevant direction directly from context examples. Consequently, we establish a test-time sample complexity that improves upon linear Transformers -- analyzed to behave like kernel methods -- and is comparable to nonlinear Transformers, which have been shown to surpass the Correlational Statistical Query (CSQ) lower bound and achieve near information-theoretically optimal rate in previous works. Our analysis reveals the crucial role of the nonlinear gating mechanism in Mamba for feature extraction, highlighting it as the fundamental driver behind Mamba's ability to achieve both computational efficiency and high performance.
items.author: Junsoo Oh, Wei Huang, Taiji Suzuki

items.title: WirelessMathBench-XL: An Auditable Benchmark for Wireless Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.23219v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Benchmarks built from arXiv papers can overlap the arXiv text used in LLM pretraining, yet technical-domain releases rarely ship the per-item evidence needed to check this. We introduce a reverse-probe n-gram audit that indexes the benchmark side and streams the corpus past it, so memory scales with the benchmark rather than the corpus and flags on the distributed problems can be inspected and recomputed. We instantiate it in WirelessMathBench-XL, a 4,027-problem benchmark for wireless mathematical reasoning built from 836 arXiv papers across 20 subfields, with multiple-choice, progressive fill-in, and full-equation-completion formats. Streaming 12.9 B RedPajama-arXiv 13-grams yields a strict zero-hit view $\mathcal{S}_0$ covering 95.7% of the problems, and shows that the Dolma and ProofPile-2 arXiv slices repackage the same RedPajama dump. Filtering to $\mathcal{S}_0$ moves every evaluated model by less than 1 pp. With 30/800 flagged test items, this comparison bounds detected-overlap inflation at 0.31-0.51 pp for frontier models rather than testing for contamination, and it does not cover paraphrase, target-answer, alternate-version, post-training, or closed-corpus exposure. Frontier models reach 86.5-91.3%, and GRPO on the released training split lifts a 7B model 25.1 pp above a size-matched general-math control. We release source-paper identifiers, per-problem audit and threshold metadata, license-aware data files, audit and bootstrap scripts, Croissant metadata, and a Datasheet.
items.author: Xin Li, Mengbing Liu, Yiyang Zhu, Wenhe Zhang, Li Wei, Jiancheng An, Chau Yuen

items.title: Machine learning approaches to seismic event classification in the Ostrava region
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.22574v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: The north-eastern part of the Czech Republic, including the Czech part of the Upper Silesian Coal Basin, is among the most seismically active areas of the country. The seismic stations in the region record mining-induced events, which continue after the cessation of mining, natural earthquakes, which are rare but may originate in the same area, and quarry blasts. A rapid and reliable distinction between the three types is required for the routine evaluation of the continuously recorded data. We study their automatic discrimination with neural networks from short three-component windows starting one second before the P-wave onset. The main data set is the archive of the Seismic Polygon Fren\v{s}t\'{a}t (1992--2002), a triggered network whose records were recovered from the original format, cleaned with deterministic and learned quality checks and completed with automatically picked P-wave arrivals; it contains about 40,000 records of all three event types. Among five compared architectures, convolutional networks operating on short-time spectrograms outperform recurrent networks operating on magnitude spectra or on the raw waveform. The best model, EfficientNet-B0 applied to 24-s windows, reaches a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.96, and blasts and natural earthquakes are practically never confused with each other; class weighting and undersampling, the usual remedies for the strong class imbalance, lower the score. Finally, we examine the transfer to the station OKC, which monitors the region today with different instruments. A model trained on the archive alone fails on the modern records, whereas a single model trained on both data sets reaches a macro-F1 score of 0.96 on the archive and 0.92 on the modern station, where the accuracy is limited by the small number of catalogued natural earthquakes rather than by the model.
items.author: Michael Skotnica, Marek Pecha, Jana Ru\v{s}ajov\'a, Bohdan Rieznikov, V\'it Wandrol, Mark\'eta R\"osnerov\'a, Jarom\'ir Knejzl\'ik

items.title: Implicit Credit Learning for Sparse-Reward Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.21828v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: When a cooperative team receives feedback only at the end of an episode, a single outcome must guide many agents' earlier actions. Learning a dense team reward helps, but its decomposition does not automatically give each agent a useful policy update. We introduce IMAP, an online method that fits a shared Q/V reward model by comparing completed episodes according to their observed terminal outcomes. Local Q/V residuals provide agent-specific rewards; the same normalized weights combine them for a centralized critic and scale local advantages for decentralized PPO actors. We characterize when these local updates follow the learned team objective. With full returns and frozen reward heads, a sharp bound relates their gradient error to variation in future Q/V compatibility; an exact identity identifies additional continuation terms for general GAE. In experiments with terminal-only feedback, IMAP's local-actor configuration attains the highest reported mean among the compared methods on all nine SMACv2 scenarios and four MAMuJoCo tasks, and on two of three SMACLite scenarios. Controlled relay interventions confirm the predicted changes in actor credit while holding the learned team reward fixed. The gradient result concerns the fitted objective; benchmark returns measure performance on the original task outcomes.
items.author: The Viet Bui, Tien Mai, Hong Thanh Nguyen

items.title: Staying in the Sweet Spot: Boost Reasoning Evolution via Responsive Rollout Difficulty Manipulation
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.06923v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has advanced the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, existing RLVR methods often suffer from exploration inefficiency due to mismatches between problem difficulty and model capability: overly difficult problems hinder reasoning path discovery, while overly simple problems offer little learning signal. To address this, we first formalize the effect of problem difficulty by quantifying the relationship between loss descent magnitude and rollout accuracy. Building on this analysis, we propose SEELE, a supervision-aided RLVR framework that dynamically adjusts problem difficulty to lie within the high-performance region. SEELE augments each training sample by appending a hint (part of a full solution) for difficulty reduction. Unlike previous hint-based approaches, SEELE deliberately computes the hint length for each individual problem to achieve an optimal difficulty. The optimal hint length is determined via multi-round rollout sampling, where an item response theory model fits accuracy-hint pairs from previous rounds to predict the next-round hint. This instance-level, real-time difficulty adjustment aligns problem difficulty with the evolving model capability, thereby improving exploration efficiency. Experiments show that SEELE outperforms Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and Supervised Fine-tuning (SFT) by +10.0 and +8.4 points, respectively, and exceeds the best prior supervision-aided approach by +3.8 points on average across six math reasoning benchmarks.
items.author: Ziheng Li, Zexu Sun, Jinman Zhao, Erxue Min, Yongcheng Zeng, Hui Wu, Hengyi Cai, Shuaiqiang Wang, Dawei Yin, Xu Chen, Zhi-Hong Deng

items.title: Challenges in Non-Polymeric Crystal Structure Prediction: Why a Geometric, Permutation-Invariant Loss is Needed
items.summary:
arXiv:2509.00832v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Crystalline structure prediction is an essential prerequisite for designing materials with targeted properties. Yet, it is still an open challenge in materials design and drug discovery. Despite recent advances in computational materials science, accurately predicting three-dimensional non-polymeric crystal structures remains elusive. In this work, we focus on the molecular assembly problem, where a set~$\mathcal{S}$ of identical rigid molecules is packed to form a crystalline structure. Such a simplified formulation provides a useful approximation to the actual problem. However, while recent state-of-the-art methods have increasingly adopted sophisticated techniques, the underlying learning objective remains ill-posed. We propose a better formulation that introduces a loss function capturing key geometric molecular properties while ensuring permutation invariance over $\mathcal{S}$. Remarkably, we demonstrate that within this framework, a simple regression model already outperforms prior approaches, including flow matching techniques, on the COD-Cluster17 benchmark, a curated non-polymeric subset of the Crystallography Open Database (COD). Our code is available at https://github.com/inria-thoth/SinkFast.
items.author: Emmanuel Jehanno, Romain Menegaux, Julien Mairal, Sergei Grudinin

items.title: Statistical Complexity of Soft Bellman Residual Minimization
items.summary:
arXiv:2508.18741v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning and offline inverse reinforcement learning aim to recover near-optimal value functions or reward models from a fixed batch of logged trajectories, yet current practice still struggles to enforce Bellman consistency scalably. Bellman residual minimization (BRM) has emerged as an attractive remedy. While globally convergent gradient-based soft (i.e., entropy-regularized) BRM methods for neural networks have recently been established, their statistical complexity under stochastic gradient descent remains largely unknown. In this paper, we address this theoretical gap for soft BRM. Through a Lyapunov-based analysis under a uniform PL condition in the auxiliary variable, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(1 / n)$ primal argument stability bound up to optimization error and an $\mathcal{O}(1 / n)$ statistical complexity for the soft BRM objective under the stated sampling conditions.
items.author: Enoch H. Kang, Kyoungseok Jang

items.title: LFM4Ads: Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation
items.summary:
arXiv:2508.14948v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent work leverages large-scale pretrained foundation models (FMs) to transfer generalizable representations to downstream advertising tasks. Most existing approaches transfer user representations (URs) and item representations (IRs), while underutilizing the user-item cross representations (CRs) generated by deeper interaction layers. Although a recent work transfers target-aware embeddings (TAEs), it requires real-time upstream FM inference alongside the downstream, introducing additional engineering complexity and overhead. To address these limitations, we propose Large Foundation Model for Ads Recommendation (LFM4Ads), an efficient pretrain-then-transfer paradigm for cross-domain ad recommendation. LFM4Ads jointly exploits URs, IRs, and CRs from the upstream FM. It extracts sample-level CRs from pretrained interaction layers and aggregates them into user-level CRs using a time-aware exponential moving average, thereby decoupling upstream inference from downstream online serving. To use CRs efficiently, we propose three downstream usages at different levels of granularity: feature-level gating to fuse CRs into downstream embeddings, module-level fine-tuning to yield downstream CRs, and model-level retrieval by matching CRs with IRs. LFM4Ads has been deployed on Tencent's advertising platform since Q4 2024. It has supported 10+ launches across major scenarios, yielding a platform-wide gross merchandise value (GMV) lift of 2.45% and annual revenue gains in the hundreds of millions of dollars. Offline experiments on KuaiRand-1K further demonstrate our effectiveness. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZhuangQu/LFM4Ads.
items.author: Jie Jiang, Shangyu Zhang, Shijie Quan, Zhongren Wang, Tianqu Zhuang, Junwei Pan, Bo Fu, Yilong Sun, Jieying Lin, Jushuo Chen, Xiaotian Li, Wenjie Li, Zhixiang Feng, Xian Hu, Huiting Deng, Hua Lu, Jinpeng Wang, Boqi Dai, Xiaoyu Chen, Bin Hu, Lili Huang, Yanwen Wu, Yeshou Cai, Qi Zhou, Huang Tang, Chunfeng Yang, Chengguo Yin, Tingyu Jiang, Lifeng Wang, Shudong Huang, Dapeng Liu, Yuekui Yang, Shu-Tao Xia, Lei Xiao, Haijie Gu

items.title: Learning Reusable Behavioral Motifs for Continuous Animal Behavior Modeling
items.summary:
arXiv:2506.15190v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Natural behavior evolves continuously and often reuses movement structure across contexts, but existing behavioral segmentation methods typically assign a single discrete syllable at each time point or impose restrictive generative assumptions. We introduce Motif-based Continuous Dynamics (MCD), a computational framework that models behavior as time-varying combinations of reusable behavioral motifs. MCD learns motifs as latent behavior-level features from transition dynamics, through spectral representation learning within a reinforcement learning framework. MCD then infers policies that combine these motifs across time or context, through offline imitation learning. This formulation avoids hard behavioral boundaries while capturing continuity and compositionality. Across simulated gridworld and continuous-control tasks, mouse maze navigation and pose data, MCD identifies reusable motifs that explain task and temporal variation. MCD therefore provides a flexible and interpretable framework for computational behavior analysis. Code is available in https://github.com/G1NO3/MCD.
items.author: Jiyi Wang, Jingyang Ke, Bo Dai, Anqi Wu

items.title: On the Depth of Monotone ReLU Neural Networks and ICNNs
items.summary:
arXiv:2505.06169v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We study two models of $\mathsf{ReLU}$ neural networks: monotone networks ($\mathsf{ReLU}^+$) and input convex neural networks ($\mathsf{ICNN}$). Our focus is on expressivity, mostly in terms of depth, and our motivation is to gain a better understanding of the depth required to exactly represent functions using neural networks with ReLU activations, a subject that has received a lot of attention lately. We prove several lower bounds on the depth required to represent functions by monotone ReLU networks and $\mathsf{ICNN}$. For the maximum function $\mathsf{MAX}_n$ computing the maximum of $n$ real numbers, we show that $\mathsf{ReLU}^+$ networks cannot compute $\mathsf{MAX}_n$, or even approximate it. We prove a sharp lower bound of $n-1$ on the $\mathsf{ICNN}$ depth complexity of $\mathsf{MAX}_n$. We also prove depth separations between $\mathsf{ReLU}$ networks and $\mathsf{ICNN}$s; for every $k$, there is a depth-$2$ $\mathsf{ReLU}$ network of size $O(k^2)$ that cannot be simulated by a depth-$k$ $\mathsf{ICNN}$. The proofs are based on deep connections between neural networks and polyhedral geometry, and also use isoperimetric properties of triangulations.
items.author: Egor Bakaev, Florestan Brunck, Christoph Hertrich, Daniel Reichman, Amir Yehudayoff

items.title: On the Adversarial Robustness of Spiking Neural Networks Trained by Local Learning
items.summary:
arXiv:2504.08897v3 Announce Type: replace
